title: Trust battery device state over UPower.onBattery

workflow: Opus full review, Sol boundary hunter, Opus self-check of the draft, editorial check, batch gates

leads.summary: At 100%, Charging state still gives contradictory panel status rows even though the hero now says Fully charged
leads.consequence: For present device state Charging and percentage=1, with either value of UPower.onBattery, batteryFull=true, charging=false, heroStatusText='Fully charged' but, once the battery-info collector has returned data, the visible stats row labels its Battery state 'Charging' and hides its rate as '-'. The new 100% assertion checks only modeLabel, not this consumer. This row mismatch also exists on the old base at this input, so it is an unresolved UI inconsistency, not solely a new regression.
leads.triage: dropped: pre-existing, identical to FullyCharged at all revisions (Opus matrix table)

leads.summary: New QML source checks pass if the old onBattery gates are accidentally restored to both charge-direction bindings
leads.consequence: The tests execute Model.js but only search Panel.qml for state-comparison substrings. A mutated Panel.qml retaining `device.state === Discharging && UPower.onBattery` and `d.state === Charging && !UPower.onBattery` passes all 28 test assertions, even though the fix's QML behavior disappears when state and global OnBattery disagree. Add tests that exercise the QML predicates via an extractable helper and cover both mismatches; regex-only checks cannot establish this behavior.
leads.triage: confirmed by coordinator source reading and Opus follow-up 1 (run 20260929T180703Z-67966c9f); published as N1 optional test note

leads.summary: Low-battery notifications still ignore a discharging battery while AC reports online
leads.consequence: The panel now shows the drain when `displayDevice.state=Discharging` and `UPower.onBattery=false` (a possibility in the UPower daemon when AC is online), but the background service's `isDischarging` returns false, so at 8% the low-battery warning remains suppressed and its notification latch is reset. Separate open PR #11161 changes precisely this predicate; this is outside the three changed files and was identified in R1.

leads.summary: Overlapping #13016 has two QML merge conflicts and a test conflict at the state-direction decision
leads.consequence: #13016 implements 30-second plug settling and branches Panel.discharging via drawingFromBattery, while this head immediately follows the battery state and expects modeLabel(Discharging,onBattery=false)='On battery' versus #13016's 'Charging'. Three-way merge produced conflict markers at Panel.qml:72-76,93-97 and power-test.sh:32-42; combined Model.js merges but cannot satisfy both existing assertions without choosing a policy. GitHub reports #13016 MERGEABLE against the base, not against this PR; these heads diverge. Coordinate the precedence and revise both sets of tests.
leads.triage: #13016 corroborates Opus / R2-F3. #9763 (PendingDischarge/rate sanitising) and #10196 (threshold argument) are ordinary overlap among ~35 PRs touching these files, not same-policy competitors; not published

leads.summary: Additional open power-panel PRs #9763 and #10196 also conflict with the changed code and fixtures
leads.consequence: #9763's modified batteryIcon() chooses the charging glyph whenever !onBattery; combined with this head's Discharging-on-AC check the head's icon test at power-test.sh:35-37 would fail if its branch wins. Its Model.js, Panel.qml and test all produce conflict markers. #10196 adds a required fourth `threshold` argument to chargeThresholdActive/batteryIcon/modeLabel; leaving this PR's 3-argument Panel calls at 52,57,74 means no threshold is ever detected, while its changed tests reject threshold with no argument and the current tests require one. Its Model.js and Panel.qml also produce conflict markers. Both PRs are still open and diverged, so avoid silently favoring either side.

leads.summary: State fixture in the changed power test assigns the wrong numeric Quickshell enum values
leads.consequence: The fixture says FullyCharged=3 and PendingCharge=4; Quickshell v0.3.1 defines 3=Empty, 4=FullyCharged and 5=PendingCharge. The tests pass because both input and expected states use the same injected map, so a plausible hard-coded state 4 for PendingCharge in Model.js would be incorrectly accepted. Update this fixture to the actual 0..6 enum and include an Empty case. This mismatch predates this revision but impacts its expanded state tests.
leads.triage: false alarm: Model.js compares states symbolically; test passes its own consistent enum object

leads.summary: A freshly charging battery with unmeasured rate/time is misidentified as a charge threshold
leads.consequence: UPower can report state Charging while EnergyRate=0 and TimeToFull=0 during its measurement delay. At 80% on AC the head's chargeThresholdActive returns true (Number(0)<=0.2), so the supposedly state-trusting UI says Threshold/Holding, shows the plain glyph and suppresses charging animation. This is a pre-existing helper issue; separate open PR #8663 addresses it, and its power-test fixture conflicts with this head's. It is not caused by the new `percentage >= 1` branch.
leads.triage: dropped: pre-existing path untouched by this PR

## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Outcome:** No defects found at 5e14e536; both points from the [previous review](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/12259#issuecomment-5860708049) are resolved as the [author's reply](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/12259#issuecomment-5861121247) describes.

| Earlier item | Status at 5e14e536 |
|---|---|
| A full battery reporting `Charging` said "Charging" | Resolved: "Fully charged" at 100%, "Charging" below |
| Icon assertion passed with two plain glyphs | Resolved: a new assertion fails on that mutation |
| First review's plug-in window and description note | Still resolved |
| Low-battery warnings follow `UPower.onBattery` (outside this PR) | Unchanged; #11161 open |
| Related open PR #13016 | Unchanged: still conflicts and expects a different `modeLabel(Discharging, onBattery=false)` |

<details><summary>Verified</summary>

- For `Charging` at 100% with `onBattery=false`, the icon, hero, info rows, pulse and profile argument now match the base branch. With `onBattery=true` the panel shows the same full battery; only the profile argument differs (`battery`), as the description intends.
- Across 2,520 synthetic inputs, the only change from e9336f97 is the hero text for `Charging` at 100%. Values just below 1 and the charge-threshold path are unchanged.
- The power tests pass at the head (28 assertions) and with the head merged into current `quattro`. The new `modeLabel` assertion fails on e9336f97.
</details>

<details><summary>Optional test improvement</summary>

The assertions on lines 66-67 of `test/shell.d/power-test.sh` only check that the state comparisons appear somewhere in `Panel.qml`. Adding `&& UPower.onBattery` back to the `discharging` binding, or `&& !UPower.onBattery` to `charging`, still passes all 28 assertions. The `discharging` gate would bring back the info-row split for the reported case, and the `charging` gate would stop the charging phrases and pulse while `onBattery` is still true. This assertion, added after line 67, fails on each of those mutants and passes at the head and with the head merged into `quattro`:

```js
assert(!/readonly property bool (?:dis)?charging: \{[^}]*onBattery/.test(panelSource), 'power panel charge direction ignores the daemon onBattery flag')
```

On the mutant with both gates restored (exit 1):

```text
ok - power panel discharging follows the device state
ok - power panel charging follows the device state
not ok - power panel charge direction ignores the daemon onBattery flag
```

At 5e14e536 with this assertion added (exit 0):

```text
ok - power panel discharging follows the device state
ok - power panel charging follows the device state
ok - power panel charge direction ignores the daemon onBattery flag
ok - powerprofiles still follow the daemon onBattery flag
```
</details>
